The statute described, which is part of the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA), establishes employer sanctions to prevent the employment of unauthorized aliens. Legally, this means that employers are prohibited from knowingly hiring, recruiting, or referring individuals for a fee if they are aware that those individuals are not authorized to work in the United States. The legal implications of violating this provision are severe, as non-compliance can result in substantial civil fines and other penalties imposed by the government. This framework places the burden on employers to verify the work authorization status of their employees, typically through the completion of Form I-9, to avoid liability.
